headline: Arista Networks has unveiled open Ethernet rack designs for AI computers, moving beyond switches.
score_reason: Pool 5 kept: an official announcement; the analysis is labelled as the columnist's view.
importance_line: What changed: Arista is moving from selling switches to selling tested rack designs, which matters most to data-centre operators and AI cloud firms that build AI clusters; the capacity and footprint claims are Arista's figures, and Arista says it has no near-term opening in Nvidia's proprietary links.
summary: SiliconANGLE reports that Arista Networks, a network equipment maker, has launched an open Ethernet rack-scale portfolio, led by Etherlink SU-144, which links up to 144 AI accelerators (specialist AI chips) in one hop, with partners including AMD, Broadcom and Meta. Zeus Kerravala, principal analyst at ZK Research, writes that the network is becoming part of the rack itself, and Arista says partners will integrate and test the liquid-cooled racks before they are delivered.
notes: Read in full. Column by Zeus Kerravala (ZK Research) written for SiliconANGLE; announcement facts and the columnist's analysis are kept apart.
